name: WPSDDC Info Vault
author: Didac Soria

sections.description:
The administration interface includes StudioDDC’s own site icon, persistent tool navigation, aligned controls and full-width text areas. It adapts to desktop, tablet and phone layouts while retaining native WordPress permissions, save actions and control colors. All presentation files ship locally; the layout does not contact an external service.

Keep a shared editorial note and a small checklist next to each piece of content. Choose which public content types use Editorial Info; all types start disabled.

  • Write a plain-text note of up to 10,000 characters.
  • Create up to 20 checklist items, mark them complete, and reorder or remove them.
  • See completion and saved-note summaries in native content lists.
  • Open the record from a native panel in the Classic or Block Editor.
  • Share each record with the people who can edit that content.
  • Save editorial information independently from content updates and autosaves.

The interface uses native WordPress controls and follows your admin color scheme. Only scoped local administration scripts and styles are loaded. No external services, telemetry or frontend output are added. No other WPSDDC plugin is required. Active collection plugins share one WPSDDC administration menu.

WPSDDC identifies the plugin collection developed by StudioDDC. This independent plugin is not affiliated with or endorsed by the WordPress Foundation or Automattic.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to wp-content/plugins and activate it.
  2. Open WPSDDC > Info Vault and select the content types you want to use.
  3. Save a new content draft first, then open Editorial Info from its editor or content list.
  4. Write your note and checklist and select Save Editorial Info.
sections.faq:
Who can see and edit a record?

People who can edit its content, using that content type’s normal permissions. The note and checklist are shared administrative information, rather than a personal notebook. The plugin does not display them on the public website or add them to public content REST responses.

How do checklist edits affect completion?

Use one distinct item per line, up to 120 characters each. Reordering an unchanged label preserves completion. Removing a line removes its item; renaming creates a new incomplete item. Save new or renamed items before marking them complete below the checklist field.

What if another editor saves at the same time?

The plugin rejects a stale form instead of overwriting the newer record. Use the back link to preserve your text, then reload the record before saving again.

What happens when I disable or remove the plugin?

Records and settings remain stored on that site. Disabling a content type keeps its records. The plugin also keeps records after content deletion, without an automatic cleanup job; deleted content has no editing link. Clear a record’s note and checklist and save while the content exists to remove that text.

Are HTML or public shortcodes supported?

No. Notes and task labels are plain text and only used in administration. No shortcode, public block or public output is registered.

Where are instructions and support?

Open WPSDDC, select this plugin and open the native Help tab at the top of its screen. Getting Started explains setup, Data and Limits explains storage and boundaries, and Support and Versions contains version details and contact links. Instructions are included and require no external manual. Support: English / Español. Following a link opens the external site; no automatic support request is sent.

What are the main operating limits?

Open Editorial Info for a supported object, add a plain-text note or checklist and save. Other users allowed to edit that object can access this information.

Data uses a local non-autoloaded option with conflict checks. It survives deactivation and can remain after related content is deleted. Clear unwanted text explicitly. Storage is not encrypted.

How are translations delivered?

English is the source language. WordPress.org supplies approved community language packs through the standard WordPress translation update system when available. StudioDDC maintains the Spanish catalog; translation catalogs are kept in the development repository and excluded from this WordPress.org plugin ZIP.
